Expanded object class, I don't like.
Just a matter of personal taste, others are free to love them. I like black licorice, so we're all wrong about something.
Only mention it because this overcame my initial negative reaction and earned the upvote.

The best part for me is the soundproofing. Taken with the smashed bulbs, that probably means that someone caused this to happen, for whatever "watch the world burn" reasons they may have.

But I find it more amusing to think this just spontaneously spawned on a random Tuesday, and the very confused building manager eventually ran out of ideas to keep all these rabid beasts nobody else ever sees out of the men's room. So he solves the problem he can and arranges it so that at least no one will be disturbed by all the roars and screaming. Maybe he also adds a bit to the janitorial budget for blood-mopping overtime.

Part of what I really like about this article is its brevity. As such, I wouldn't want to add too much in terms of additional content that helps make a crosslink work. A simple footnote would suffice. The article mentions that the creatures summoned by the bathroom are large mammals, why not a footnote giving a brief list of examples, one of which was an instance of SCP-1000 which, you know, was a large mammal. As such, I am proposing the following edits:

Changing this:

Should the above conditions be met at any time, one or more instances of SCP-984-1 will materialize inside SCP-984 once a person exits a stall. Specimens of SCP-984-1 tend to be large, highly aggressive mammals of varying species. All SCP-984-1 specimens disappear nine minutes after manifestation. SCP-984-1 will not willingly leave SCP-984 for any reason, and will disappear if it is forced to do so.

To this:

Should the above conditions be met at any time, one or more instances of SCP-984-1 will materialize inside SCP-984 once a person exits a stall. Specimens of SCP-984-1 tend to be large, highly aggressive mammals of varying species.1 All SCP-984-1 specimens disappear nine minutes after manifestation. SCP-984-1 will not willingly leave SCP-984 for any reason, and will disappear if it is forced to do so.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

Footnotes
1. Specimens have included Canis lupis, Alces alces, Ursus arctos, and in one case an instance of SCP-1000.
